title: Police defend officer who shot knife-wielding man
article: A police officer who shot and killed a Calgary man was justified in his actions, a fatality inquiry heard Monday.
Const. Ian Vernon killed Harjinder Singh Cheema with a single bullet after Cheema stabbed his wife and mother-in-law repeatedly with a knife on Jan. 21, 2005.
Cheema came out of his southeast Calgary home, approached police with a large kitchen knife in his hands and refused to drop the weapon.
Const. Steve Adair testified he was also aiming his gun at Cheema and was prepared to take the shot, but was concerned about hitting the homes behind Cheema if he missed.

Using a baton or pepper spray was not an option because Cheema had a deadly weapon, said Adair, who defended Vernon's actions. The police onthe scene were not equipped with Tasers, a weapon designed to cause temporary paralysis.
Vernon was absolved by police of any wrongdoing in the incident, but a fatality inquiry is automatic in these kinds of cases.
Cheema's former wife, Kuldeep Sandhu, also testified.
She filed for divorce earlier that Januaryafter Cheema got drunk and threatened to kill their two-year-old daughter with a knife, she said.

On the day Cheema was shot by police, he confronted her about her divorce application, then stabbed her 32 times in the head, chest and arms. He also stabbed hermother before turning the knife on himself.
Speaking outside court, Sandhu said police, whom she had first contacted months before the attackabout her husband's behaviour, offered her enough help.
"Police helped me lots," she said. "My community, they didn't help me or anything."
The inquiry is scheduled to last for two weeks.
